THE EVERYDAY CHALLENGE

StepAble starts
with a real need.

A task described as one instruction—“do the laundry”—contains many smaller decisions. Support needs can vary by task, environment, and day, so guidance should be adjustable rather than fixed.

Offer the amount of guidance a person chooses, with a clear way to repeat, pause, or ask for help.

HOW IT COULD WORK

A thoughtful path
through the moment.

This walkthrough illustrates the intended experience. It describes the product direction, not functionality available on this website.

  1. Choose a familiar activity

    Begin with a defined household routine or an errand to prepare for. The intended experience would account for the person’s environment and preferred level of support.

  2. Move one step at a time

    Follow a picture or spoken instruction, repeat it, or request more detail. Optional camera assistance is an area to explore, not a working capability.

  3. Adjust the support

    Keep helpful prompts and reduce unnecessary ones as confidence develops. Any caregiver access would be optional and permission-controlled.

PLANNED CAPABILITIES

The details
we’re exploring.

  • Break cooking, cleaning, laundry, and organization into understandable steps.
  • Offer picture-based and spoken instructions.
  • Explore optional camera-based assistance for recognizing objects.
  • Adapt the pace and complexity of guidance.
  • Help prepare for errands and using public transportation.
  • Offer optional caregiver support with explicit permissions.
  • Reduce prompts as the person becomes more confident.

AN EVERYDAY EXAMPLE

What support could look like.

A laundry routine could guide someone through sorting, loading, choosing settings, and putting clothes away, with additional visual guidance when requested.

A design consideration

The direction is to develop with input from people with disabilities and relevant specialists. StepAble would support how to do a task; AddvancedFocus focuses on choosing and starting it.

ACCESSIBILITY & CONTROL

Designed around
the person using it.

Picture-based and spoken guidance, adjustable pace, large usable controls, and repeatable steps would support different cognitive and motor needs.

Privacy, affordability, and user autonomy are shared Biro.dev design principles. Product-specific data practices, supported access methods, and any offline capabilities would be explained before public release.

Read our design commitments

QUESTIONS ABOUT STEPABLE

A clearer picture.

How is this different from AddvancedFocus?

AddvancedFocus centers on deciding what to do and getting started. StepAble would focus on understanding how to carry out a chosen activity, step by step.

Would a caregiver need to monitor every task?

Constant supervision is not the goal. The right level of support depends on the person and the activity; optional caregiver roles would need careful design.

Could camera guidance handle any activity?

No such capability is promised. Camera interpretation can be wrong, and the suitability of an activity would need to be assessed as part of development.

When can I use StepAble?

StepAble is in early concept development. There is no public release date, price, or supported-platform list yet. The next step is to develop and evaluate the intended experience.
